complexity.notes: The annotation tuple(int) is invalid typing syntax (should be tuple[int, ...]); also word_tuple is recomputed for every word in both passes, and a collections.defaultdict(list) would avoid the double computation and the redundant dict-comprehension pass. Worst case assumes adversarial hash collisions degrade dict lookups to O(n) each.
complexity.summary: Each word is mapped to a 26-element letter-count tuple used as a dict key; words sharing a key are appended to the same group. Since word lengths are bounded by a constant, all work is linear in the number of words.
